target_customer: Residential roofing contractors, mostly small and mid-size, who pay a monthly software subscription and per-report fees
problem: Roofers lose time and jobs measuring roofs by hand and producing slow, plain proposals. Roofr turns satellite and aerial imagery into measurement reports and polished proposals within minutes.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for roofers plus per-report measurement fees
product_category: Vertical SaaS for roofing sales (measurements, proposals, CRM)

founders.name: Richard Nelson
prior_employers: A larger roofing company (sales role, name not stated)
founders.background_notes: Third generation roofer who grew up in the family roofing business and worked as an installer (Roofr About page, YC page).

founders.name: Kevin Redman
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO on the Roofr About page and in TechCrunch 2021; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Early product combined satellite imagery with manual roof drawing and templated proposals, mostly standard web engineering. Automated measurement later added harder computer vision work.

defensibility.rationale: Imagery was licensed from third parties such as Nearmap and the proposal workflow was copyable. The edge was domain insight and a cheap price against EagleView, and later CRM data and distributor integrations raised switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge. TechCrunch in 2021 listed Roofer Pro, RoofSnap and AccuLynx as similar software vendors, and Roofr kept raising through 2025.

market_need_then: Roofers paid roughly tens of dollars per EagleView-style report and quoted slowly. Roofr's 2019 release positioned it against paid lead services. No dated 2017 demand statistics were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses roofr.com, the exact .com. Acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Roofr icon plus wordmark in Roofr Blue (Pantone 2130C) and a light blue; brand kit forbids gradients on the full logo
identity.voice_and_tone: Built for roofers, by roofers; practical and contractor friendly

branding.community_and_virality: Company runs a roofer podcast and blog on branding for roofers; no evidence of merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear niche brand with a registered ROOFR mark (2019), a published brand kit and a founder story that resonates with contractors, but no evidence of mass virality.

pivots.from: Marketplace connecting homeowners with roofing contractors (Product Hunt 2017 listing)
pivots.to: Sales software for roofers with measurement reports and proposals
pivots.why: Not stated by a source I opened; the 2019 release shows the company already selling contractor tools.

outcome_analysis: Roofr started in 2016 with a roofer founder and a marketplace framing, completed YC in 2017 and raised a 2019 seed from Crosslink. It then focused on measurements, proposals and a CRM for roofers, raising a second seed in 2021, a Series A in 2022, a 23.5 million round in 2023 and a TCV-led Series B in 2025. Distributor ties with ABC Supply show a defensible niche, though rivals like AccuLynx and EagleView remain large.
notes: Competitors left empty: no source dated near the 2017 batch names rivals; the TechCrunch 2021 article (Roofer Pro, RoofSnap, AccuLynx) and 2026 comparison pages are too late.
